Lab 8 will be based on an IN CLASS discussion of various papers. I have found several recent studies comparing various variant calling workflows (as a way of going beyond GATK, which we have covered in class). I will assign multiple students to read EACH paper before class . We will have an activity in class based on your reading that will require you to have a good understanding of the paper assigned for class. Below are the assignments for this in class activity. Since you will be preparing for the activity, please make sure to attend class on the Lab Day to get credit for Lab 8 since we will not have an out of class component (meaning it will be due in class as part of the activity).

## Guiding Questions for Reading:
- What are the main goals of the pipeline evaluations in the paper?
- Which aligners and variant callers are compared, and what are their strengths/weaknesses?
- What are the key findings regarding accuracy, speed, and robustness?
- How do the papers address biases or limitations in variant calling?
- Are the recommendations from the paper applicable to different research contexts?

## In-Class Lab: Comparing Variant Calling Workflows
### Overview:
In this class, you will work in groups to analyze and compare different variant calling workflows based on pre-assigned papers. Be prepared to discuss key findings, compare methodologies, and brainstorm how to apply these workflows to non-model systems.

### What to Expect:
1. Small Group Synthesis (20 min):

- Meet with others who read the same paper.
- Summarize key recommendations and how they were determined.
- Create a workflow diagram (drawn on a whiteboard).

2. Group Presentations (15 min):

- Each group will give a brief (2-3 min) summary of their paper.

3. Cross-Group Discussion (20 min):

- Mix into new groups where each student brings insights from a different paper.
- Compare tools, datasets, and strengths/weaknesses across studies.

4. Case Study Challenge (15 min):

- Brainstorm how to design a variant calling benchmark for a non-model system or other application.

5. Wrap-Up Discussion (5 min):

- Reflect on which workflows were most reliable and identify gaps in current methods.

## Preparation:
- Review your assigned paper using the guiding questions provided.
- Be ready to discuss, compare workflows, and contribute to group diagrams.

## Assignment:
- Submit a screenshot/photo of your workflow diagram in Canvas after class.
- Grading is participation-based—no written report required.
